content.title: About
content.content: Turkey wing is a piece of poultry meat that contains both protein and a modest amount of fat. When boiled, the skin becomes soft and edible, while the meat stays tender and mildly flavored. Wings are commonly used in soups, stews, or served as a standalone dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turkey wings are rich in collagen, which supports skin and joint health.
In the United States, turkey consumption spikes around holidays, especially Thanksgiving.
The skin of turkey contains more fat than the meat, but boiling releases some of it into the broth, enhancing flavor.
Turkey wings are popular in Asian cuisines for making stocks and sauces.
There are many preparation methods: from simple boiling to roasting with spices.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: Turkey wing provides about 20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which are important for metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Essential minerals
items.content: Wings supply iron, zinc, and phosphorus, needed for blood formation and bone health.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Ideal for low‑carb diets as it contains virtually no sugars.

items.title: Collagen and gelatin
items.content: The skin releases gelatin during cooking, which can benefit joints and digestion.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to turkey meat.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If the wings are seasoned with salt, they can become a source of excess sodium.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Undercooked meat may harbor Salmonella or Campylobacter; proper cooking temperatures are essential.

items.title: Fat in the skin
items.content: Consuming large amounts of skin can increase the calorie density of the dish.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Turkey wings can be enjoyed hot or cold. They are often served as an appetizer, sliced into bite‑size pieces. The skin is edible after boiling and adds a pleasant texture. Pair them with yogurt‑based dips, mustard, or soy‑based sauces for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked wings in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a sealed bag for 2‑3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C before serving.
